subject.title: Backup: add encrypted snapshot backup flow

question: Should OpenClaw core accept a native folder-backed encrypted snapshot and destructive restore flow with new backup config, once the security blockers and proof gap are fixed?
rationale: The branch creates a new secrets-bearing backup surface and restore path that can rewrite OpenClaw state, credentials, config, and workspaces, so implementation correctness alone does not settle the product and security boundary.

options.title: Require hardened native flow
options.body: Keep this PR open only if the branch is rebased, the security findings are fixed, no-op config is removed or implemented, and real CLI proof is supplied before final review.

options.title: Split hardening from feature
options.body: Ask for a smaller PR that improves the existing archive create/verify path while the snapshot product direction remains undecided.

options.title: Defer native snapshots
options.body: Close or pause the core PR and rely on existing local archives or external backup tools until maintainers sponsor the native snapshot direction.

recommendation.title: Require hardened native flow
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open only if the branch is rebased, the security findings are fixed, no-op config is removed or implemented, and real CLI proof is supplied before final review.

likelyOwner.reason: The current main backup CLI/archive files most clearly route through Vincent Koc's recent backup-area history.
